messages:
anya: Quick design proposal — add a small "bridge-service" that performs envelope rewrites for legacy clients so the gateway can forward a single canonical payload shape. Keeps gateway thin and avoids embedding a ton of brittle conditionals.

liam: high level — bridge runs as a shared cluster service or per-tenant sidecar?

anya: prefer shared first (cheap), but opt-in per-tenant via `X-Bridge-Enabled: true`. Start shared + strict resource limits.

noah: shared reduces ops but increases blast radius. We need circuit breakers and a per-tenant rate cap; also isolation for noisy tenants.

rachel: observability checklist — preserve original request id, add `bridge.request_id`, emit latency breakdown (gateway->bridge->runtime), and tag transform failures `bridge.transform_error`. Also add sample payloads to S3 for debugging (redacted).

liam: implementation tradeoffs: rule engine as JSON mapping vs small DSL vs WASM. JSON table-driven is easiest to patch, WASM gives safety/perf but is heavier to ship.

anya: prototype rule example below (very small):
```
{"from":"legacy.v1","to":"core.v2","map":{"user_id":"headers.x-user","prompt":"body.text","stream":"body.options"}}
```
We'd apply path mapping, optional defaulting, and small validators.

noah: perf note — target p50 < 5ms added latency. If we do complex JS transforms it'll spike. Lean native (Go) rule evaluator with compiled paths. Consider a guarded WASM path for rare complex cases.

rachel: security note — bridge must not decrypt or inspect encrypted blobs. Auth passthrough only; validate JWT scopes and forward `Authorization` intact. Any transform that requires secret access must be rejected.

liam: rollout plan suggestion: 1) dry-run mode that logs what would change (header `X-Bridge-Dry: true`), 2) canary tenants with sampling 1%, 3) automatic rollback on >0.5% transform errors or >30ms median added latency.

anya: agree. Also add an operator toggle in console per-tenant and a feature flag for dry-run. Minimal config schema for rules and a REST endpoint to PATCH rules.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary cluster available in staging for bridge v0.1 — build #3421 queued. :shipit:

noah: testing — we need a small harness: run legacy client traffic through staging bridge and diff outputs with native gateway passthrough. Add fuzz tests for path mapping and null fields.

rachel: metrics to track: transformed_requests_total, transform_failures_total, added_latency_ms histogram, drop_reasons (validation, timeout, auth). Dashboards + alert when failures spike.

liam: ops cost — estimate 2 nodes at 4 vCPU each to start for staging canary, autoscale by CPU/queue depth. Keep memory low.

anya: action items: (1) spike rule engine (Go table-driven) — @liam, (2) infra for canary cluster + limits — @noah, (3) observability schema + alerts — @rachel, (4) playground + dry-run logs — @anya. We'll reconvene after spike in 4 business days.

rachel: SGTM. :+1:

liam: I'll open the RFC PR with the prototype API for rules.

anya: thanks all — adding notes to the infra runbook and will post a short blurb in #eng-platform when canary is live.
